criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The mission purpose, measurable preliminary objectives, intended operator and customer groups, and their needs are clearly connected. The rationale is supported by relevant references. The optical payload and feasibility of detecting coral colour at the proposed resolution remain to be developed, so the concept is not yet fully validated.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef, so that bleaching is detected within days instead of after a seasonal aerial survey.
Objectives 1 and 3 come directly from the managers' need to react within days, and objective 2 from the researchers' need to see individual reefs.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A clear Gantt chart is linked to the mission’s design sequence, with task descriptions, relevant information sources, and practical contingencies for access, coverage, schedule, and competing deadlines. The plan is robust and feasible; some technical decisions and task-level deliverables remain open, appropriately for this preliminary stage.

evidence.quote: The order follows the mission: the imaging requirements (objectives 1 and 2) fix the orbit altitude and local time, so orbit work comes before ground control and communications, whose contact times depend on the chosen orbit.
The main risks and the planned responses are listed in Table 1.
Table 2 lists the sources I plan to use and what each is for.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: The report includes useful orbit calculations for altitude, period, orbit count, sun-synchronous inclination, ground-track shift, and swath, with an interpretation that identifies the coverage trade. The calculations are broadly sound and progress is evident, though the STK result is only briefly reported and no access or payload-performance analysis is yet shown.

evidence.quote: I have also made first hand calculations for a candidate orbit, a circular sun-synchronous orbit at 600 km altitude (Table 3)
A first STK scenario with this orbit has been set up, and its period agrees with the hand calculation.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report has a logical structure, readable prose, clearly labelled figures and tables, and a consistent overall presentation. In-text citations correspond to a reference list. Some online references are bibliographically vague or incomplete, and occasional awkward phrasing prevents the report from being fully polished.

technical_issues.issue: The proposed 10 m visible-band coral-colour imaging is not supported by a defined sensor or an assessment of water-column attenuation, depth, turbidity, cloud, and atmospheric correction; these factors can limit bleaching detection.

The orbit calculations are broadly plausible, but the stated swath and equatorial ground-track shift do not demonstrate weekly access to the reef. The submission appropriately identifies coverage as unresolved and should verify it through access simulations and a repeat-cycle analysis.

overall: A strong preliminary report with a well-defined Australian mission concept, a robust project plan, relevant sources, and credible initial orbit work. The main design challenge is demonstrating that the proposed optical observations can detect bleaching at the required resolution and revisit rate.

feedback.summary: You present a strong preliminary report: the Australian reef-monitoring mission is tied to user needs, your project plan is feasible and includes contingencies, and your orbit calculations show useful technical progress. To strengthen the design, verify that the proposed optical observations can detect bleaching under realistic conditions and demonstrate that the orbit provides the required reef access and revisit rate.
next_steps: Define a candidate sensor and test whether 10 m visible-band imaging can detect coral bleaching at relevant depths, accounting for water attenuation, turbidity, cloud and atmospheric correction.
Use access simulations and repeat-cycle analysis to verify weekly access to the reef; report the results and connect them to your coverage requirements and orbit trade-offs.
Develop the Figure 1 plan with clear task deliverables and checkpoints, and polish the report by completing online reference details and reviewing awkward phrasing.

criteria.C1: Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly connects measurable objectives to reef managers’ and researchers’ needs, with relevant references. To make the concept more fully validated, define the sensor and assess whether bleaching is detectable at the proposed resolution under realistic water, cloud and atmospheric conditions.
criteria.C2: Your Project Plan links the Gantt chart (Figure 1) to the mission design sequence, identifies useful sources and includes contingencies. To make the plan more robust, specify task-level deliverables and checkpoints, and show how access and coverage analysis will resolve the weekly-revisit requirement.
criteria.C3: Your Preliminary Progress includes plausible calculations for orbit altitude, period, inclination, ground-track shift and swath, plus an initial STK check. Build on this by simulating reef access and repeat cycles, then interpret whether the orbit meets weekly coverage needs; also begin assessing payload performance.
criteria.C4: Your report is logically structured, readable, and uses labelled figures and tables; in-text citations correspond to the reference list. For a more polished presentation, complete bibliographic details for online sources and revise occasional awkward phrasing.
